title: Patch: joining a game checks the deck against the cards the server already holds, instead of copying all 978 cards through JSON first
thread:
**Issue #4518 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4518: Patch: joining a game checks the deck against the cards the server already holds, instead of copying all 978 cards through JSON first
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The server checks that a player's deck is legal every time they join the queue, open or join a room, pick a deck in a lobby, or send, post or accept a daily challenge. To do that check, it first writes a full text copy of every card in the game (all 978) and reads it straight back, and only then looks at the deck itself. The check alone takes about a hundredth of a millisecond. The copying takes about 9 milliseconds on a fast machine, and the live server runs on a quarter of one processor, shared with every match being played. Once this is built, the server checks the deck against the cards it already holds in memory. Players get exactly the same answers, refusal messages included, a little sooner, and live matches stop waiting behind it.

## Why

- `crates/server/src/api/decks.rs:1166` `assert_legal` builds a `serde_json::Value` of the whole catalog (`to_json(&app.catalog.defs)?`, line 1178). It wraps that in a second `json!` value, parses it back into `validator::DeckInput` or `LoadoutInput` with `serde_json::from_value` (1188, 1194), turns the typed `LoadoutResult` back into JSON (1191, 1199), and then walks that JSON by key to rebuild the refusal (1202 to 1229).
- The validator needs no owned copy. `check` in `crates/engine/src/validator.rs:229` takes references and reads only `catalog.cards` and `catalog.banned`. Only the public `validate_deck(&DeckInput)` and `validate_loadout(&LoadoutInput)` (185, 211) wrap an owned `CatalogSnapshot`, and they exist for the browser module's JSON entry points (`crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs:761-766`).
- The catalog is 978 cards, 575,855 bytes as minified JSON (`crates/cards/catalog.json`).
- Measured with a scratch release build (thin LTO, as the workspace's release profile has it) on a 4-core CI runner, 50 calls per run, three runs:
  - today's path: 8.70 to 8.77 ms per call
  - a typed call that clones the catalog: 0.38 ms
  - the engine's check alone: 0.012 ms
- It runs on every `freeze_choice` (`decks.rs:1279`, `1296`). The callers are `api/queue.rs:333` (queue join), `actor/rooms.rs:396, 483` (room create and join), `lobby/mod.rs:803` (every lobby pick), `daily/invites.rs:200, 286, 419` (daily challenge, seek, accept) and `duos/rooms.rs:119` (co-op room).
- It runs inline on a tokio worker, unlike the engine's other heavy calls (`engine::off_runtime` in `api/practice.rs:201` and `daily/games.rs:184`). The server is one `basic` container (`wrangler.jsonc:40-41`, `max_instances: 1`), so the sockets and match actors on that worker wait for it.

## Proposal

1. **Engine.** `check` takes the card list and the ban list as borrows. Add two public entry points that borrow them, for example `validate_deck_in(deck: &LoadoutDeck, cards: &CardDefs, banned: &[CardId], collection: &Collection) -> LoadoutResult` and `validate_loadout_in(decks: &[LoadoutDeck], ...)`; the names are the builder's choice. `validate_deck` and `validate_loadout` delegate to them unchanged, so the browser module and the bot pool (`crates/shared/src/bots/pool.rs`) behave as before.
2. **Server.** `assert_legal` builds each `LoadoutDeck` as `deck_at` does today (`name: Some(deck.name.clone())`, the saved cards), turns the owned counts into a `Collection`, and calls the new entry points with `&app.catalog.defs`. It reads the typed result: `ok` decides; otherwise the message is the first error's and `details` is `serde_json::to_value(&result.errors)`. `LoadoutError` serializes to exactly the keys the JSON walk copies today (`rule`, `message`, and `deck` and `cardId` when present), so the 409 `loadout_invalid` body stays byte for byte the same.
3. **Ban list.** Keep today's list: the catalog ids `Catalog::is_banned` marks, in catalog order, as line 1172 builds it. Do not switch to `Catalog::snapshot()`'s raw list, so the L6 messages cannot change.
4. **Owned counts.** The store answers `i64` and the validator's `Collection` holds `i32`. Today a count above `i32::MAX` fails the JSON parse and answers 500. Decision: saturate (`i32::try_from(n).unwrap_or(i32::MAX)`), since a count that large already owns every copy L5 can ask for. Rejected alternative: keep the 500. No real account reaches this case.
5. At 0.012 ms the check needs no `off_runtime`.

Rejected alternatives:
- Build a typed `DeckInput` from `app.catalog.snapshot()`. It needs no engine change, but it still clones all 978 card definitions per call (0.38 ms measured).
- Keep a second `CatalogSnapshot` on `App`. That holds a second copy of every card definition for the life of the process.

## Where it lands

- `crates/engine/src/validator.rs` (`check` and the two new entry points); `crates/engine/tests/rules/validator.rs`
- `crates/server/src/api/decks.rs` (`assert_legal`, lines 1166 to 1239, which get shorter); `crates/server/src/api/catalog.rs` only if the ban list is computed once at boot
- SPEC §9.4 is unchanged: one validator, shared by client and server, still runs at queue time. No ruling, since no rules decision is made. If `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` §6 or `crates/engine/README.md` lists the validator's entry points, the new ones join that list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `crates/server/src/api/decks.rs` no longer turns the catalog into a `serde_json::Value`: no `to_json(&app.catalog.defs)`, and no `serde_json::from_value` into `DeckInput` or `LoadoutInput`.
- [ ] The engine has the borrowing entry points, and `validate_deck` and `validate_loadout` delegate to them. An engine test shows both forms answer the same `LoadoutResult` for a legal deck, a legal trio, each of L1 to L6 failing, a banned card and an unowned card.
- [ ] A server test calls `freeze_choice` (or the queue route) with a legal deck, a legal trio, and decks and trios failing each rule, a banned and an unowned card among them. It holds each refusal's message and `details` (rules, messages, `deck`, `cardId`, their order) to today's answers.
- [ ] The existing loadout tests pass unchanged: `crates/server/tests/api/decks.rs`, `tests/api/catalog.rs` and `tests/api/queue.rs`.
- [ ] The pull request gives the time per call before and after, from a release build. This is a one-off measurement, not a checked-in timing test.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' validator`, `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, and so does the web's WebAssembly size test (`apps/web/src/wasm/size.test.ts`).

## Size and risks

Small: about 40 to 80 lines across two crates, with fewer lines in `decks.rs` than today. `difficulty:medium`: it adds to the engine's public validator surface but decides no rule.

Risks:
- A refusal's `details` could change shape. The equivalence test and the existing loadout tests guard against that.
- The validator also ships in the browser module. Two thin delegating functions barely move its size, and the size test holds it.

## Plan

_Written by `gpt` (codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45077662363)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Make queue/room deck validation borrow the server’s in-memory card definitions instead of serializing and reparsing the full catalog. Preserve the browser/shared owned-input APIs and every legal result and `loadout_invalid` refusal (message, ordered details, and optional `deck`/`cardId` fields), keep bans in catalog order, saturate out-of-range owned counts, and record a release-build before/after timing without checking in a benchmark.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/engine/src/validator.rs` | change | Add `validate_deck_in` and `validate_loadout_in`; make `validate_deck`/`validate_loadout` delegate and split `check`’s borrowed catalog inputs. |
| `crates/engine/tests/rules/validator.rs` | change | Prove owned-input and borrowed-input results are identical for legal inputs and every L1–L6/banned/unowned case. |
| `crates/server/src/api/decks.rs` | change | Rewrite `assert_legal` to construct typed decks/collection and consume typed `LoadoutResult` without catalog JSON round trips. |
| `crates/server/tests/api/decks.rs` | change | Exercise `freeze_choice` for legal deck/trio choices, all applicable L1–L6 refusals, bans, unowned cards, error shape/order, and saturated counts. |

Do not touch `crates/server/src/api/catalog.rs`, `crates/wasm/core`, `crates/shared`, `apps/web`, catalog data, configs, docs, spec/ruling files, migrations, or forbidden `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, and `.claude/` paths. SPEC §9.4 and existing R164/R253 govern the behavior; no rule changes and no new ruling is required. `crates/engine/README.md` names `validator::*` generically and `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` documents the unchanged WASM entry point, so neither needs an edit.

## Steps

1. In `crates/engine/src/validator.rs`, add public `validate_loadout_in(decks: &[LoadoutDeck], catalog_version: &str, cards: &CardDefs, banned: &[CardId], collection: &Collection) -> LoadoutResult` beside `validate_loadout`, and `validate_deck_in(deck: &LoadoutDeck, catalog_version: &str, cards: &CardDefs, banned: &[CardId], collection: &Collection) -> LoadoutResult` beside `validate_deck`. Include `catalog_version` because L6’s unknown-card message contains it; do not add another catalog/view type.
2. In the same file, make `validate_loadout` pass `&input.catalog.version`, `&input.catalog.cards`, `input.catalog.banned.as_deref().unwrap_or_default()`, and `&input.collection` to `validate_loadout_in`; make `validate_deck` do the corresponding delegation; leave `validate_trio` delegating through `validate_loadout`. Change private `check` to accept those borrowed pieces plus `Scope`, build its `IndexSet<&str>` from the supplied ban slice, and replace all `catalog.cards`/`catalog.version` reads with `cards`/`catalog_version`. Do not change traversal, error ordering, messages, or serialization types.
3. In `crates/engine/tests/rules/validator.rs`, import `DeckInput`, `validate_deck`, `validate_deck_in`, and `validate_loadout_in`. Add `borrowed_entry_points_match_owned_inputs_for_legal_and_every_l1_l6_result`: compare `validate_deck` with `validate_deck_in` for one legal fixture deck, compare `validate_loadout` with `validate_loadout_in` for `legal_loadout()`, then compare the two loadout paths for every `INJECTIONS` entry. This table already covers both L1 variants, both L2 variants, L3 duplicate/token, L4, L5 unowned, L6 unknown, and L6 banned; compare the complete `LoadoutResult`, not only rules.
4. In `crates/server/src/api/decks.rs::assert_legal`, retain the current ban derivation semantics by iterating `app.catalog.card_ids`, filtering with `Catalog::is_banned`, and cloning only matching IDs into `Vec<validator::CardId>` in catalog order. Do not call `Catalog::snapshot()` or use `app.catalog.banned` directly.
5. Still in `assert_legal`, convert `owned: &IndexMap<String, i64>` directly into `validator::Collection`, cloning IDs and mapping each quantity with exactly `i32::try_from(*quantity).unwrap_or(i32::MAX)`. Build each `validator::LoadoutDeck` with `name: Some(deck.name.clone())` and `cards: deck.cards.clone()`; for `LoadoutScope::Deck`, preserve the current empty fallback with `LoadoutDeck::default()` and validate only the first supplied deck via `validate_deck_in`; for `Trio`, collect every supplied deck and call `validate_loadout_in`. Pass `&app.catalog.version`, `&app.catalog.defs`, the ordered bans, and the typed collection. Do not use `to_json(&app.catalog.defs)`, `json!`/`serde_json::from_value` for validator inputs, clone a `CatalogSnapshot`, or move the check to `off_runtime`.
6. Consume the returned `LoadoutResult` directly: return success when `result.ok`; otherwise require `result.errors.first()` as today, clone its `message`, serialize `&result.errors` once with the existing `to_json` helper, and pass that value unchanged to `ApiError::with_details(ApiErrorCode::LoadoutInvalid, ...)`. Keep the existing internal error for an empty refusing result. Remove only imports made unused by this rewrite (`Map` remains needed by `record_of`).
7. In `crates/server/tests/api/decks.rs`, import `Catalog`, `DeckInput`, `LoadoutDeck`, `LoadoutInput`, `LoadoutResult`, `validate_loadout`, `TestAppOptions`, and `test_app_with` alongside the existing test imports. In `freeze_choice_r253_what_a_ticket_or_a_room_keeps`, add helpers `validator_collection`, `expected_deck_result`, `expected_trio_result`, and `assert_refusal_matches`. They must construct the existing owned `DeckInput`/`LoadoutInput` with `app.catalog.snapshot()`, compare a `freeze_choice` error’s 422 `loadout_invalid` code, first-error message, and `error.details == Some(to_json(&expected.errors))`, thereby pinning rule/message/`deck`/`cardId` fields and their order to the unchanged browser-facing path.
8. Add test `r253_borrowed_validation_preserves_legal_choices_and_every_l1_l6_refusal`. Use direct fake-store saves, the existing `saved_deck`, `legal`, `own`, `save`, and `freeze` helpers, and 75 distinct playable IDs. Assert a legal Bo1 deck and legal three-deck Bo3 trio freeze unchanged. Against isolated setups, cover Bo1 L2 short, L3 duplicate (own two), L5 unowned, L6 unknown (own the unknown ID), and L6 banned; cover Bo3 L1 empty slot, L2 short, L3 duplicate, L4 shared card across two decks (own two), L5 unowned, L6 unknown, and L6 banned. For banned cases, create the app with `test_app_with(TestAppOptions { catalog: Some(Catalog { banned: vec![victim.clone()], ..base.catalog.clone() }), ..Default::default() })`, then seed the two active profiles as `setup` does. Each refusal must match the corresponding owned validator result through `assert_refusal_matches`, not merely contain a rule.
9. Add test `owned_counts_above_i32_max_saturate_for_validation`. Store `i64::from(i32::MAX) + 1` for one card used by an otherwise legal Bo1 deck (and normal ownership for the rest), then assert `freeze_choice` succeeds. This proves the specified saturation instead of preserving the former JSON-parse 500.
10. After tests are green, create a scratch Cargo project under `/tmp/jackioh-4518-bench` (never in the repository) with path dependencies on `jackioh-engine` and `jackioh-cards`, `serde_json` with `float_roundtrip`, `indexmap` with `serde`, release `lto = "thin"`, and a driver that uses one legal 25-card deck/full 978-card `CATALOG`. In three runs of 50 iterations each, time with `Instant` and `black_box`: (a) the old `to_value` + `json!` + `from_value::<DeckInput>` + `validate_deck` + result JSON/error-walk pipeline reproduced from the pre-change `assert_legal`, and (b) typed deck/collection construction + `validate_deck_in` + error serialization. Run `cargo run --release --manifest-path /tmp/jackioh-4518-bench/Cargo.toml`, record every run and per-call before/after values in the pull-request report, and remove the scratch directory. Do not add a timing assertion or benchmark file to the repository.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/rules/validator.rs::borrowed_entry_points_match_owned_inputs_for_legal_and_every_l1_l6_result`: full-result equivalence for legal deck/trio and all fixture injections. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' validator`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/decks.rs::freeze_choice_r253_what_a_ticket_or_a_room_keeps::r253_borrowed_validation_preserves_legal_choices_and_every_l1_l6_refusal`: legal freezes and exact typed refusal parity. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::decks::freeze_choice_r253_what_a_ticket_or_a_room_keeps`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/decks.rs::freeze_choice_r253_what_a_ticket_or_a_room_keeps::owned_counts_above_i32_max_saturate_for_validation`: overflow ownership saturation. Run the same focused server command, then run the acceptance crate suite `cargo test -p jackioh-server`.
- Run `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/wasm/size.test.ts`.
- Run the harness checks `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, and `cargo jackioh spec check`, then `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`.

## Done when

- [ ] The server validator path performs no full-catalog JSON conversion or typed-input `from_value` and borrows `app.catalog.defs`.
- [ ] Both public borrowed engine entry points exist, while owned APIs, WASM calls, and bot-pool calls remain source- and behavior-compatible.
- [ ] Ban membership comes from `is_banned` in catalog order; counts beyond `i32::MAX` saturate; no runtime offload or second resident catalog is added.
- [ ] Legal deck/trio results and every L1–L6, unknown, banned, and unowned refusal retain complete typed results and server message/details order and shape.
- [ ] Focused engine/server tests, full server crate tests, combined clippy, rustfmt, WASM size, catalog, patches, spec, and classification checks pass; generated web wire files remain unchanged.
- [ ] Three 50-call thin-LTO release measurements report before and after per-call times, with no benchmark artifact left in `git status`.

## Risks

- Serializing `LoadoutError` directly could alter optional fields or ordering; compare the complete error vectors and server details to the unchanged owned/WASM path, and use the existing derived serializer without a hand-built map.
- Using `Catalog::snapshot()` would clone 978 definitions and using its raw ban vector would violate the requested adapter semantics; pass `defs` by reference and derive only the ordered banned IDs.
- An unchecked `i64 as i32` can wrap and falsely reject ownership; use the specified checked conversion and saturation test.
- The engine API ships in WASM even though bindings do not change; keep the old wrappers and run the size test. This refactor touches no game state, RNG, replay, hidden information, migration, or client rule enforcement.

## Open questions

None. The borrowed API names are fixed above; `catalog_version` is retained to preserve L6 text, and the issue already decides saturation, ban ordering, and no `off_runtime`.
```
